extracted.intended_audience: scientific journal peer reviewers (researchers serving as reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers on how to write constructive, professional peer reviews for scientific journals, including what to include, what to avoid, and implicit norms of reviewer conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall summary and journal appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall summary of the paper's main contribution and journal appropriateness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin the review with a concise statement of the manuscript's main contribution and whether the scope/quality of the work fits the target journal. This orients editors and authors to your assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize major revision items
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize major revision items needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly list the substantive problems that must be addressed for the paper to be publishable (e.g., missing experiments, fundamental methodological issues, misinterpretation of results). These should be prioritized and separated from minor points.

rubrics_metrics.name: List minor suggestions separately with specific line numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: List minor suggestions separately with specific line numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep minor edits (typos, small clarifications, formatting, small wording changes) distinct from major revision items and reference specific line or page numbers so authors can locate and act on them easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on the research, not author attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the research itself, not author attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the manuscript's claims, methods, evidence, and presentation rather than speculating about or criticizing the authors' background, identity, or motivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use third-person, depersonalized language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use third-person language to avoid sounding accusatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrase critiques about the work (e.g., 'The manuscript does not demonstrate...' rather than 'You failed to...'). Depersonalized wording improves professionalism and reduces perceived hostility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific examples with citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific examples with citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending changes or critiquing prior work, cite relevant literature and give concrete examples (e.g., ``The analysis in Figure 2 lacks X; see Smith et al. 2020 for an alternative approach'').

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer actionable feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer "actionable feedback" that guides authors constructively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete, feasible suggestions for how authors can address problems (e.g., suggest types of additional analyses, clearer wording, or experiments) rather than only stating that something is inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread review for bias before submitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread your review for bias before submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform a self-check for potential conscious or unconscious bias (gendered language, cultural assumptions, tone) and revise wording to be fair and evidence-based before finalizing the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague statements without elaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Make vague statements without elaboration. (DON'T)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not give unexplained judgments such as 'This is unclear' or 'Not convincing' without specifying why and how to improve; provide examples and actionable steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid commanding or accusatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use commanding or accusatory language. (DON'T)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from imperative or blaming phrasing (e.g., 'You must do X', 'This is wrong') that can sound confrontational; prefer neutral, constructive phrasing focusing on the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include gendered or derogatory remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Include gendered or derogatory remarks. (DON'T)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never make comments that demean or stereotype based on gender, race, nationality, or other protected characteristics. Such remarks are unprofessional and unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not equate language proficiency with scientific quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume language proficiency reflects scientific quality. (DON'T)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate assessments of scientific rigor from authors' English proficiency; suggest language edits or professional editing if needed but do not penalize scientific contributions based on writing alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inflammatory assumptions without evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Make inflammatory assumptions without evidence. (DON'T)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base criticisms on evidence in the manuscript or literature; avoid conjecture about motives, data fabrication, or misconduct unless there is clear support and you follow journal procedures for reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not question authors' qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Question authors' qualifications. (DON'T)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the work on its merits rather than critiquing the authors' credentials, affiliations, or experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include personal attacks on character
rubrics_metrics.description: Include personal attacks on character. (DON'T)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ad hominem remarks or insults. Focus comments on the manuscript and its improvement; personal attacks are unprofessional and harm the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not allow unconscious bias to influence recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow unconscious bias to influence recommendations. (DON'T)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively consider and correct for possible implicit biases (e.g., against certain institutions, countries, or demographic groups) when forming evaluations and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose and avoid conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceed if conflicts of interest exist without disclosure. (DON'T)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a financial, personal, or professional conflict (collaboration, close relationship, competitive interest), disclose it to the editor and recuse if appropriate; do not review while conflicted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate major vs minor items and reference line numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete review separates major-vs-minor items and references specific line numbers. (Implicit norm)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the review so editors/authors can see which issues are deal-breakers versus minor corrections; include line/page references for each point to facilitate revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic phrasing as part of review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Linguistic phrasing is part of review quality (depersonalize, third-person, no accusation). (Implicit norm)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone and phrasing affect how feedback is received; craft sentences to be neutral, professional, and focused on the manuscript to increase the utility and fairness of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer self-audit for bias as workflow step
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer self-audit for bias is part of the workflow, not optional. (Implicit norm)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate an explicit bias check into your review workflow (e.g., scan for gendered language, check whether criticisms would apply regardless of authors' identities) before submitting.
